decision: resolve_doc_search_root owns the pattern base. docs_path set: patterns are relative to it. docs_path "." is stored distinct from "" and means the library root. No docs_path and any pattern that names a path (not "**/"-prefixed): match from the root. No docs_path and every pattern "**/"-prefixed (the defaults): auto-discover the docs directory. An index that matches zero files raises before scope reconciliation, so the library ends in status error and keeps its last good chunks.
title: Docs library include_patterns match against a base chosen by one rule
why: Auto-discovery used to narrow any empty docs_path to a discovered docs/ directory, so root-relative patterns (docs/**/*.md, README.md) matched nothing and the library reported ready with 0 files (/observablehq/plot, /typst/typst, Magic UI's dead registry pattern, 2026-09-26). Stored rows materialize the default patterns, so "were patterns given" cannot be recovered from the DB; whether a pattern names a path can. Switching every custom-pattern library to the root was rejected: all-"**/" sets such as neo4j GDS **/*.java would expand to the whole repository. A dry run against the cached clones changed only Magic UI's file set.

decision: search_codebase computes upstream's indexed_names only after the source coordinator declines; the source lane's resolved mode uses _resolve_mode(query, mode) without names. Native symbol, path and hybrid lanes keep upstream's validated identifiers, the not-the-named-symbol marking and their hints.
title: The source lane routes on query shape; only native lanes read the wiki symbol table
why: Upstream v0.54 loaded the wiki's symbol names before routing every query, which made the source lane depend on the wiki store and added a read to each query; under the fork's test stubs the lane failed outright. Absorbed 2026-10-01 in b38f0cdec; the base-vs-tip unit suites fail the same 37 environment-pin tests and nothing new, and Infra's consumer contract passes 20/20 on the served engine.

decision: apply_revert_supersession (through _live_records) and apply_head_artifact_check select only DecisionRecord.source != 'journal'. Revert retirement never writes a journal row's status, and artifacts_gone is never derived for journal rows, matching the existing staleness exclusion; accepted_decision_ids passes journal confirmations through _row_currency and HISTORY_CURRENCIES.
title: Journal rows keep journal lifecycle under upstream's revert and head-artifact passes
why: Upstream v0.54 added revert-based supersession and an artifacts_gone history lane that would otherwise write status or move a confirmed journal decision to history outside the JSONL authority (absorb invariant 11). Verified 2026-10-01 in merge f993251e2: a copy of Infra's 133-record journal reads identically through the merged code and the base.
